system_description.narrative_title: A Tightly Coupled World: Security Shocks, Trade Frictions, Financial Stress
system_description.narrative_summary: The global geopolitical order is an open, tightly coupled system under stress: concurrent security shocks (Middle East attacks, Russia-Ukraine), rising economic friction (trade disputes, export surges and industrial competition), and volatile financial markets (bond sell-offs, currency moves) interact and amplify one another. Weakening of maritime governance, targeted sanctions and protectionist industrial policy are re-routing supply chains and reshaping alliances, while domestic political polarization in Europe and elsewhere increases the probability of disruptive policy shifts. These feedbacks — commodity-price spikes raising inflation, markets repricing sovereign risk, and security escalations disrupting trade — make the system more brittle and more prone to cascade effects.
system_description.scope: Nation-states, alliances and blocs, non-state armed actors, global trade and maritime routes, finance and capital markets, critical supply chains (energy, minerals, tech), international institutions and public opinion that mediate their interactions.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio-economic-environmental system (the globalized political-economy embedded in resource, climate and demographic constraints).
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy & maritime logistics subsystem (oil/gas markets, tankers, canals, shipping governance)
International financial markets & capital flows (sovereign debt, bond markets, FX, cross-border lending)
High-tech and critical-minerals supply chains (chips, batteries, AI infrastructure, rare minerals)

variables.name: US–China strategic tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting trade, technology and critical‑industry supply chains—driven by US export controls and tariffs and China’s push in chips, AI and export growth—shaping a deepening economic and technological decoupling.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and campaign of strikes
variables.description: Russia’s large‑scale military campaign against Ukraine and Kyiv’s asymmetric responses, amid sustained Western arms, finance and diplomatic support and intermittent peace efforts, are driving volatile frontlines and prolonged strategic competition in Europe.

variables.name: US–Iran escalation and regional maritime attacks
variables.description: The United States and Iran, together with Iranian‑aligned proxies (notably Houthi forces), are engaged in a cycle of strikes on vessels, energy infrastructure and military targets that is intensifying Gulf security tensions and threatening global energy flows.

variables.name: Israel–Palestine confrontation and settlement diplomacy
variables.description: Israel and Palestinian actors are locked in a high‑intensity political and security confrontation—including settler expansion, Gaza aftermath and cross‑border strikes—prompting new sanctions, diplomatic ruptures and shifts in Western and regional policy responses.

variables.name: Global financial and market stress
variables.description: A reordering of global finance is underway as rising bond yields, abrupt currency moves (notably the yen), central‑bank interventions and growing cross‑border capital flows (including offshore renminbi borrowing) reshape sovereign financing costs, corporate borrowing and monetary policy space.
